title: Self-organized quasicrystals and their excitations in dipolar Bose-Einstein condensates via optical feedback
authors: Liang-Jun He, Fabian Maucher, Yong-Chang Zhang
abstract: Quasicrystals emerge from competing interactions with incommensurate characteristic length scales that inhibit translational periodicity. Here, we show that such multiscale interactions can be realized in a dipolar Bose-Einstein condensate through the interplay between intrinsic dipole-dipole interactions and photon-mediated interactions generated by coupling to an excited-state manifold together with a suitably engineered optical feedback. This interplay gives rise to two pronounced roton instabilities in the Bogoliubov excitation spectrum, leading to a rich ground-state phase diagram including dodecagonal quasicrystals with twelvefold rotational symmetry for experimentally realistic parameters. We further propose a protocol to access these quasicrystals dynamically and develop a general numerical framework for calculating their collective excitation spectra.
summary: The paper theoretically investigates the formation of self-organized quasicrystals in dipolar Bose-Einstein condensates by coupling dipole interactions with engineered optical feedback. It predicts a rich phase diagram featuring dodecagonal QCs and develops advanced numerical methods to calculate their unique excitation spectra. This work demonstrates how quantum control over long-range interactions can stabilize exotic, non-periodic crystalline phases.
main_problem: The primary goal is realizing and characterizing self-organized quasicrystals (QCs) within a controllable quantum system.
main_result: The study predicts the existence of dodecagonal QC states in dipolar Bose-Einstein condensates, characterized by unique excitation spectra and finite superfluid fractions.
method: The research employs mean-field theory, solving the Gross-Pitaevskii Equation (GPE) reformulated in 4D momentum space using a projection method to analyze ground states and excitations.
model_or_system: The system is a quasi-2D dipolar Bose-Einstein condensate (dBEC). QC formation arises from the interplay between intrinsic dipole-dipole interactions and effective long-range oscillatory interactions generated via optical feedback.
key_observables: Bogoliubov excitation spectrum, ground-state phase diagram showing transitions to dodecagonal QCs, superfluid fraction $f_s(r_\perp)$, and characteristic gapless modes (phasons).
important_parameters: Interaction ratios ($a_s/a_{dd}$), condensate density ($ho_{2D}$), detunings ($\Delta_\pm$), and the ratio of excitation momenta $ ar{k}_2/ ar{k}_1 	o \sqrt{2} + \sqrt{3}$.
main_assumptions: The system is treated in a quasi-2D limit using a Thomas-Fermi profile, and calculations for QCs rely on projecting the problem into 4D momentum space due to lack of translational periodicity.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the experimental setup (optical feedback), the ground-state phase diagram showing QC regimes, the convergence of QC peaks in momentum space towards ideal ratios, and the dynamic evolution protocol for generating QCs.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the physical mechanism (DDI + optical feedback) to deriving the effective GPE. It then analyzes the resulting ground-state phase diagram, calculates the excitation spectrum using advanced projection methods in momentum space, and finally proposes a dynamic quench protocol for realization.
why_interesting: This work bridges concepts from quantum optics (optical feedback), many-body physics (BECs), and condensed matter theory (quasicrystals) to predict novel quantum phases of matter that are highly tunable via external fields.
